claims.rule: On a touch screen, every control a component draws (its button, action, dismiss or close control) can be pressed anywhere in a target at least 44 by 44 points (CSS pixels on web).
claims.why: A smaller target is missed by people with a tremor or limited dexterity, and by everyone on the move.

evidence.finding: Targets under 44 by 44 fail WCAG 2.5.5 (level AAA, chosen on purpose above 2.5.8's AA floor of 24) and Apple's HIG minimum (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Buttons-and-controls).

checks.web: registry/ouro/components/ouro/button/button.touch.test.tsx measures the Button's box on a coarse pointer, and the Toaster test "gives the dismiss and action buttons 44px touch targets". Not yet checked on web: the Sheet's close control and the Alert's dismiss button. The web checks for text-field are not yet listed here. The web checks for segmented-control, checkbox, sync-status are not yet listed here.
checks.apple: TouchTargetTests (Tests/OuroHXTests/ComponentTests.swift) read every button size's and every close control's minimum target; the gallery's ComponentClaimTests.testEveryControlIs44Points measures every button's frame on every component page, and testEveryComponentPagePassesTheAccessibilityAudit runs performAccessibilityAudit, whose hitRegion audit fails a small target. The TextField: TextFieldMetricsTests.aTextFieldIsATouchTarget asserts 44 and 56 points tall, and testEveryControlIs44Points measures its Clear and Show password buttons on the gallery's textfields page. The SegmentedControl, Checkbox and SyncStatus: ChoiceMetricsTests asserts segments 44 points tall on touch and the checkbox row 44 points; testEveryControlIs44Points measures them and the sync line's Retry on the gallery's choices and sync pages.

claims.fix: Give the control a 44-point minimum frame and content shape on touch platforms, even when it draws smaller.

claims.rule: With Reduce Motion on, a component animates no movement: no slide, scale, spring or bounce. What would move crossfades instead, over `ouro.duration.base`, and a press does not scale. A drag may still follow the finger, since the person is moving it.
claims.why: Movement across the screen can make people with vestibular disorders dizzy or sick.

evidence.finding: WCAG 2.3.3, and Apple's HIG on Motion (https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/motion): motion triggered by interaction must be possible to turn off, unless it is essential, as following a finger is.

checks.web: The Button test "does not scale with reduced motion", the Sheet test "drops transform motion under reduced motion and keeps an opacity fade" and the Toaster test "slides on the ease-out curve in 300ms or less, never animates height, and only fades with reduced motion". Not yet checked on web: the Alert. The drag allowance: the Toaster test "still follows the finger with reduced motion, then returns or fades with no travel". The web checks for skeleton are not yet listed here. The web checks for segmented-control, checkbox, sync-status are not yet listed here.
checks.apple: ComponentMotionTests (Tests/OuroHXTests/ComponentTests.swift) read each component's transition and press scale with reduceMotion true and false: a crossfade with it on, never a move or a scale. The Skeleton: LoadingMetricsTests.aSkeletonHoldsStillUnderReduceMotion asserts it never breathes under Reduce Motion. The SegmentedControl, Checkbox and SyncStatus: ChoiceMetricsTests asserts no press scale or thumb slide under Reduce Motion, and SyncStatusTests asserts the saving arrows hold still (OuroSyncStatusMetrics.spins).

claims.fix: Pick the animation from the Reduce Motion setting: OuroMotion's step on Apple, `motion-reduce:` on web.

claims.rule: Every control has a name a screen reader speaks and the role it plays (button, heading); a component's title is a heading; decorative icons are hidden from the screen reader.
claims.why: A control without a name is announced as "button" or skipped, so a blind person cannot tell what it does.

checks.web: The Empty test "renders the title as an <h3>, the description, the icon and the action", the Alert test "shows a dismiss button with onDismiss, named by dismissLabel" and the Sheet test "renders a Close button last in the sheet, hidden until keyboard focus, that closes it" query by role and name; the axe lane checks names. Not yet checked on web: the Badge, the Card and the Item. The web checks for text-field, avatar, page-header, skeleton, spinner, progress are not yet listed here. The web checks for separator, description-list, segmented-control, checkbox, sync-status are not yet listed here.
checks.apple: The gallery's ComponentClaimTests.testVoiceOverLabels finds each control by its VoiceOver label as a button, each title as text, and no decorative icon; testEveryComponentPagePassesTheAccessibilityAudit runs performAccessibilityAudit's sufficientElementDescription and trait audits on every page. The Badge: testVoiceOverLabels reads a recipe row on the gallery's badges page as one element that says its badges' words and not their decorative icons, and finds no badge as a button. The Card: testVoiceOverLabels reads the cards page's titles and description as text and its action as a button. The Item: testVoiceOverLabels reads a pressable row on the items page as one button named by its title and description, its action as its own button, and no decorative icon. The TextField, Avatar, PageHeader, Skeleton, Spinner and Progress: testVoiceOverLabels finds each on its gallery page by its spoken name (a field by its label and never its placeholder, the header's title and its actions, the spinner by its label); AvatarMetricsTests.anAvatarIsNamedByItsPerson, TextFieldMetricsTests.theHintReadsTheErrorThenTheDescription and LoadingMetricsTests.aBarSaysHowFarAlong assert the rest. The Separator, DescriptionList, SegmentedControl, Checkbox and SyncStatus: testVoiceOverLabels finds each on its gallery page by its spoken name (a separator's label as text, each pair as its term then its details, each segment by its word, the checkbox by its label with its value, the sync line by its words); DisplayMetricsTests, ChoiceMetricsTests and SyncStatusTests assert the rest.

claims.fix: Pass a visible title or an explicit accessibility label; mark titles as headers; hide decorative images.

claims.rule: At the largest text size the platform offers (Apple's accessibility sizes, 200% text on web), titles, messages and action labels wrap onto more lines; none is truncated or clipped.
claims.why: People who need large text lose the words that tell them what an action does when a label is cut off.

checks.apple: The gallery's ComponentClaimTests.testEveryComponentPagePassesTheAccessibilityAudit launches every component page at accessibility XXXL and runs performAccessibilityAudit, whose textClipped and dynamicType audits fail clipped or fixed-size text. The Badge: BadgeMetricsTests (Tests/OuroHXTests/ComponentTests.swift) checks it keeps one line only up to the largest standard size and wraps at every accessibility size, and the audit runs on the badges page. The Card: CardMetricsTests checks its title and description have no line limit and its action goes under the title at the accessibility sizes. The Item: ItemMetricsTests checks the same for a row, whose actions go under its words and whose picture goes above them; the audit runs on the cards and items pages. The TextField, the PageHeader and the Progress: PageHeaderMetricsTests.aPageHeaderReflows asserts no line limit on the title; the field's label, description and error and the bar's label set no line limit and grow vertically (fixedSize). The DescriptionList, SegmentedControl and Checkbox: DisplayMetricsTests asserts the list stacks below its breakpoint and at the accessibility sizes, ChoiceMetricsTests that the segments stack at the accessibility sizes; the checkbox's label and description set no line limit.

claims.fix: Let labels wrap (no fixed line limit at accessibility sizes, no fixed heights) and use text styles that scale.

claims.rule: Text and icons that carry meaning reach 4.5:1 against what is behind them in every theme, light and dark, and 7:1 when the platform's increased-contrast setting is on.
claims.why: Low-contrast text cannot be read by people with low vision, or by anyone in sunlight.

evidence.finding: WCAG 1.4.3 (4.5:1 for text) and 1.4.6 (7:1, the enhanced level). Ouro chooses 7:1 for increased contrast, and holds meaningful icons to the text ratio, above 1.4.11's 3:1 for graphics.

checks.web: The axe lane's color-contrast rule, 4.5:1 in light and dark. Not yet checked on web: 7:1 under increased contrast. Not yet checked on web: the Badge, the Card and the Item. The web checks for text-field, avatar, page-header, progress are not yet listed here. The web checks for separator, description-list, segmented-control, checkbox, sync-status are not yet listed here.
checks.apple: ContrastTests (Tests/OuroHXTests/ComponentTests.swift) compute the WCAG ratio of every component's text and icons on its surface, every tone and variant, in all six themes, light and dark, standard and increased contrast; performAccessibilityAudit's contrast audit runs on the gallery. ComponentSnapshotTests keeps references of every component in light, dark and increased contrast. The Badge: ContrastTests' everyBadgeLabelReadsOnItsFillInEveryThemeAndMode covers every tone and variant, and aBadgeTakesTheButtonsColours checks it uses the button's palette. The Card: ContrastTests' cardTextReadsInEveryThemeAndMode covers both variants and the edge. The Item: itemTextReadsInEveryThemeAndMode covers a row's words, its icon tile's symbol and the lines between rows. The TextField, Avatar, PageHeader and Progress: ContrastTests resolve their palettes in every theme and mode, asserting 5:1 text (7:1 under increased contrast), the field's edge and the bar's fill at 3:1, and every avatar hue. The Separator, DescriptionList, SegmentedControl, Checkbox and SyncStatus: ContrastTests resolve their palettes in every theme and mode, asserting 5:1 text (7:1 under increased contrast) and the checkbox's edge and tick at 3:1.

claims.fix: Take text colours from the theme's foreground pairs, and raise them under increased contrast (OuroColor.increasedContrast on Apple).

claims.rule: A banner or toast is announced once when it appears. A destructive banner or toast interrupts what the screen reader is saying, and so does a warning banner; the others, warning toasts included, wait their turn.
claims.why: A message that is never announced is never heard, and one that always interrupts trains people to ignore it.

evidence.finding: WCAG 4.1.3 asks for status messages a screen reader announces without moving focus.

checks.web: The Alert test "uses role=%s for a %s alert" (alert.test.tsx, an it.each: destructive and warning give role=alert, the rest role=status) and the Toaster test "is announced once, its message and description only: politely, and a destructive toast assertively (Review Focus 5)". Not yet checked on web: that a warning toast waits its turn. The web checks for sync-status are not yet listed here.
checks.apple: AnnouncementTests (Tests/OuroHXTests/ComponentTests.swift) read each tone's announcement priority for a banner and for a toast. The SyncStatus: SyncStatusTests asserts a problem is spoken when it starts and saved when one clears, and nothing else (OuroSyncStatusMetrics.announcement), posted politely.

claims.fix: Announce on appear with the tone's priority for that component: role=alert or role=status on web, AccessibilityNotification.Announcement with a priority on Apple.

claims.rule: A toast with an action stays until it is dismissed, unless the app gives it a duration; one without an action dismisses itself after 5 seconds by default.
claims.why: A timed Undo can run out before a keyboard, switch or screen reader user reaches it.

checks.web: The Toaster test "keeps a toast that has an action until it is dismissed, unless duration is given".
checks.apple: ToastTests (Tests/OuroHXTests/ComponentTests.swift) resolve each toast's duration: nil (until dismissed) with an action, 5 seconds without one, the app's duration when given; the gallery's ComponentClaimTests.testAToastWithAnActionWaits sees a plain toast leave and the Undo toast stay.

claims.fix: Leave the duration unset on a toast with an action, or pass one long enough to reach it.

claims.rule: A sheet, a dismissible banner and every toast have a close control with a name, which a screen reader can reach and press.
claims.why: On a phone a screen reader user has no Escape key and may not know the dismiss gesture, so without a control they are stuck.

evidence.finding: WCAG 2.1.2: focus that cannot leave a component traps the person in it. VoiceOver's escape gesture (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/objectivec/nsobject-swift.class/accessibilityperformescape()) exists, but many people never learn it, so the control is the reliable way out.

checks.web: The Sheet test "renders a Close button last in the sheet, hidden until keyboard focus, that closes it", the Alert test "shows a dismiss button with onDismiss, named by dismissLabel" and the Toaster test "closes from the dismiss button".
checks.apple: The gallery's ComponentClaimTests.testCloseControlsClose finds the sheet's, the banner's and a toast's close control by its label, presses it and checks the surface is gone.

claims.fix: Render a labelled close button ("Close", "Dismiss") inside the surface.
